principle: Drift and false-green are the maximum risk. Prefer the option that closes test blind spots and holds safety gates uniformly. Safe-side default; never resolve an asymmetry by loosening the strict side.

decisions.title: install-skill does not copy the _shared/kiwi mirror (tool gap)
decisions.recommend: a-sequenced (register SRS requirement now + fix test-first as the NEXT unit, not bundled into the current commit); b (register-and-defer) is the acceptable safe fallback; reject c (manual workaround)
decisions.rationale: Confirmed in code: collectSharedResourceReferences (install-skill.ts:402-425) validates that ../_shared/kiwi/* references EXIST in the source and records them in metadata, but copyPackageTo (488-497) copies only files inside the single skill directory. The _shared/kiwi mirror is NEVER copied to the destination. So an install to any fresh location (a project without a pre-existing _shared mirror) produces a BROKEN skill whose ../_shared/kiwi/* references dangle -- this is a real correctness defect, not merely latent drift. The test suite hides it twice: (1) install-skill.test.ts:244-268 records sharedResourceReferences in metadata but never asserts the destination _shared mirror was materialized; (2) install-skill.test.ts:307-314 only asserts referenced _shared files EXIST under .agents/skills/_shared/kiwi (green solely because those files are checked into this repo) and never compares their CONTENT to skills/codex/_shared/kiwi. A source _shared edit that leaves the mirror stale is therefore false-green. Option c (manual sync) is the single worst risk choice -- unenforced manual mirror upkeep is precisely how silent stale drift is born, and it violates the CLAUDE.md mandate 'record the gap as SRS work before relying on manual workarounds'. The fix MUST be test-first and its acceptance criteria MUST include a source-vs-destination _shared content-parity assertion (closing the false-green blind spot). Do not ram a new feature fix into the same commit as the current 11 implemented reqs.
decisions.execution_note: Register a v2.3.0.1 SRS requirement: install-skill SHALL materialize/refresh the destination _shared/kiwi mirror for every scoped-runtime install, with AC mandating (a) the mirror is copied on install/update and (b) an automated test comparing source _shared content to destination _shared content (EOL-agnostic). Implement test-first (red: install to a fresh temp dest that lacks _shared, assert broken/repaired). Until fixed, keep the checked-in .agents/skills/_shared/kiwi mirror under version control -- never a manual out-of-band sync process.
decisions.fidelity_impact: high -- closes a silent stale-drift and broken-install blind spot in the skill mirror, directly serving the project purpose (SRS-fidelity vs code drift).

decisions.title: -qna / --qna footgun (one-dash typo can flip behavior)
decisions.recommend: a (complete the deprecation: rename/remove the deprecated --qna alias) -- but the load-bearing control is fail-closed parsing: any unrecognized or single-dash variant MUST hard-error, never silently produce the opposite behavior
decisions.rationale: --qna is already a deprecated alias (scheduled removal by v0.11) and QnA is now default-on, so the alias carries little value while presenting a footgun: a one-character typo (-qna vs --qna, or a mistype toward --auto semantics) that silently flips whether the interactive QnA gate runs. From the risk lens the blast radius is LOW and RECOVERABLE (you observe QnA didn't run and re-invoke), so this is not a must-fix-now emergency. The genuine hazard is a SILENT opposite outcome; the fix that eliminates it is not documentation but fail-closed argument parsing -- unknown/mistyped flags must error out, not degrade to a default that happens to be the inverse of intent. Documenting (b) alone leaves the silent-flip live. A rename is a user-facing behavior change and therefore needs SRS + TDD; since the alias is already on a deprecation path, folding the footgun removal into that deprecation is the clean, low-risk move.
decisions.execution_note: Under SRS + TDD: remove/rename the deprecated --qna alias on its scheduled deprecation and add a test asserting that -qna (single dash) and any unknown flag produce a structured error (fail-closed), never a silent QnA-off/opposite run. Low priority relative to D1/D4.
decisions.fidelity_impact: medium -- prevents a silent intent-inversion but on a recoverable, low-blast-radius surface.

decisions.title: FR-FLOW-029 --wt (half-specified option: reintroduce vs keep removed)
decisions.recommend: b (keep removed for v2.3.0.1); reintroduce ONLY later via a fully-specified requirement + AC + test (a done properly), never half-specified
decisions.rationale: As written, FR-FLOW-029 (kiwi-wave-master) is internally consistent WITHOUT --wt: neither the Requirement text nor AC-1..AC-5 mention it, and the code has no --wt. That is zero SRS-vs-code drift -- the safest possible state. Reintroducing a HALF-specified --wt (no crisp AC, ambiguous worktree/isolation semantics) manufactures exactly the SRS-says-X / code-does-Y divergence this project exists to prevent; a partially-specified option is a drift magnet and an untested surface. Feature absence (b) has no ambiguity, no false-green, no maintenance surface. Note the requirement is also Stability=evolving with all AC still unchecked and only a plan-type VE -- adding a new half-baked option now would compound unverified surface. If --wt is genuinely wanted, it must land as option a executed fully (amend requirement + author complete AC + add test) in a future cycle, not be resurrected in a partial state at a commit boundary.
decisions.execution_note: Leave --wt out; keep FR-FLOW-029 as authored (no --wt) so SRS and code stay byte-consistent. If reintroduction is desired, open it as new fully-specified SRS work with its own AC and TDD; do not reintroduce without a complete AC.
decisions.fidelity_impact: high -- preserves exact SRS/code consistency; blocks reintroduction of a drift-prone under-specified surface.

decisions.title: hot-fix -> srs-sync --auto-apply propagation asymmetry (dry-run/approval gate bypass)
decisions.recommend: a (align to the SAFE side -- forbid auto-apply bypass of the dry-run + user-approval gate UNIFORMLY across all agent variants) AND record as SRS (d). Reject b (allow on codex/etc) and reject c (document-only).
decisions.rationale: This is the highest-severity item for the risk lens. kiwi-srs-sync's contract is 'dry-run 선행 의무 + 사용자 승인 후 MCP mutation' -- a mandatory review gate protecting the SRS SSOT from unreviewed mutation. An --auto-apply that skips that gate is a SAFETY-GATE DEFEAT that writes to the source of truth without human review = direct drift/corruption of the SSOT, the exact failure mode the project fights. The asymmetry (claude forbids, codex/etc allow) is worse than a uniform policy because the same logical operation carries different safety guarantees depending on runtime -- a surprise vector. The cardinal risk-lens rule: resolve an asymmetry by tightening to the strict side, NEVER by loosening the strict side. Therefore align everyone to claude's forbid (a). Option b (allow on codex/etc) expands the gate-bypass surface = worst choice. Option c (document-only) leaves the bypass live -- documentation does not stop a bypass. SRS capture (d) is required regardless because this is a behavior change needing spec coverage and TDD. Also consistent with CLAUDE.md's prohibition on bulk-finalize/auto flips of SRS state without per-item evidence and gate checks.
decisions.execution_note: Under SRS + TDD: make the dry-run + approval gate uniform across claude AND codex/etc/all variants -- --auto-apply (or --auto) must NOT skip the dry-run/approval step before MCP mutation. Add a test asserting that on every agent variant an auto path still surfaces a dry-run and requires explicit approval before mutation. Do not add an allow-path for codex/etc.
decisions.fidelity_impact: high -- restores a uniform safety gate preventing unreviewed SRS SSOT mutation.

decisions.title: Follow-up: commit / verified transition / push / exit
decisions.recommend: COMMIT now (yes). Do NOT transition reqs to verified (keep implemented). PUSH: feature branch only, decoupled from verified transition (acceptable as backup). EXIT: fine after commit.
decisions.rationale: COMMIT: 11 implemented reqs + analysis artifacts + skill changes are all uncommitted (git status). Uncommitted work is the 미커밋 유실 risk; committing is low-risk and fully recoverable via history. Commit FIRST, before any other motion. VERIFIED TRANSITION: strongly against now. verified is a high-bar, trust-signaling, effectively-irreversible state that tells future agents 'done and proven'. Current evidence does not justify it: e.g. FR-FLOW-029/030 are Stability=evolving, every AC checkbox is unchecked ([ ]), and the only Verification Evidence is a plan-type reference (VE-1 -> a plan doc), not a passing-test result. A plan reference is not verification. CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids bulk-finalize flipping multiple reqs to verified without per-requirement evidence and stability-gate checks. Bundling a verified sweep into a wrap-up motion is the classic false-green risk -- keep at implemented; transition per-req only when real test evidence exists and the stability gate passes. PUSH: publishing to a shared remote is outward-facing and costly to rewrite, but this is a feature branch (feat/2.3.0.1), not a protected branch, so pushing it as backup/collaboration is acceptable -- provided it is NEVER to main/protected and is decoupled from any verified transition. EXIT: fine once committed.
decisions.execution_note: Sequence: (1) commit all current work to feat/2.3.0.1 (recover 미커밋 risk); (2) leave all reqs at implemented -- no bulk verified transition (per-req evidence + stability gate required first); (3) optionally push feat/2.3.0.1 as backup (never protected branch, never coupled to verified); (4) exit. Keep the D1/D4 fixes as separate TDD units after commit.
decisions.fidelity_impact: high -- prevents premature verified false-green while eliminating uncommitted-loss risk; keeps evidence integrity of the completion signal.

overall: The dominant risks are safety-gate defeat (D4) and silent stale-drift/false-green (D1), both of which corrupt the source of truth the project protects -- so both get safe-side, gate-holding, blind-spot-closing recommendations and the highest fidelity weight. D5 must keep the verified signal honest (no bulk transition without per-req evidence) while committing immediately to remove uncommitted-loss risk. D3 favors zero SRS/code drift (keep --wt absent). D2 is a real but recoverable footgun whose true fix is fail-closed parsing, not documentation. Cardinal rule applied throughout: tighten asymmetries to the strict side, never loosen; prefer the option that fills the test blind spot; never rely on unenforced manual sync.
